sources.excerpt: Lunastone Pedals Launches The Three Stage Rocket MIDI: A Deep Dive for Guitarists and Pro Audio Engineers | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / guitars guitars Lunastone Pedals Launches The Three Stage Rocket MIDI: A Deep Dive for Guitarists and Pro Audio Engineers By Liam Carter July 9, 2026 Lunastone Pedals has officially launched the Three Stage Rocket MIDI — a paradigm-shifting 3-channel analog gain pedal engineered for professional players who demand precision, repeatability, and seamless integration with digital workflows. Unlike conventional multi-gain pedals that compromise tone or routing flexibility, the Rocket MIDI features three independent, hand-tuned analog circuits (Overdrive, Distortion, Fuzz), each with discrete JFET and op-amp stages, true bypass switching, and full MIDI 1.0 implementation via 5-pin DIN and USB-C ports. Measuring 126 mm × 114 mm × 68 mm and weighing 520 g, it ships with a rugged, CNC-machined aluminum chassis, custom-molded rubber feet, and gold-plated PCB edge connectors. Firmware version 1.3.2 (released 17 April 2024) adds SysEx patch dump support, bi-directional expression mapping, and compatibility with Line 6 HX Stomp, Fractal Audio Axe-Fx III, and Strymon Timeline firmware v5.02+. Engineering Philosophy: Analog Integrity Meets Digital Precision Lunastone’s design team — led by founder and former Bogner engineering lead Elias Vargas — spent 22 months developing the Rocket MIDI’s signal path. Every channel uses discrete-component topology: no digital modeling, no DSP-based clipping, and zero digital audio conversion in the core signal chain. The Overdrive channel employs a dual-JFET front end (2N5457 and PN4393) followed by a low-noise OPA2134 op-amp buffer; the Distortion channel features cascaded BC549C transistors with adjustable clipping symmetry via trimmer potentiometers; the Fuzz channel uses germanium diodes (OA91) and NKT275 transistors wired in a modified Tone Bender MkIII configuration. Signal-to-noise ratio is measured at ≥98.2 dB (A-weighted, 1 kHz, unity gain), and THD+N remains below 0.012% up to +12 dBu input level — verified using Audio Precision APx555 test suite. This commitment to analog purity extends to power management. The Rocket MIDI accepts 9–18 V DC center-negative (2.1 mm × 5.5 mm barrel), with internal voltage regulation delivering stable ±15 V rails to critical op-amps and ±9 V to transistor stages. Independent low-dropout regulators (TI TPS7A4700 for positive, TPS7A3301 for negative) ensure noise floor consistency regardless of supply voltage — confirmed across tests from 9.0 V to 17.8 V DC. Current draw is 192 mA at 12 V, rising to 238 mA at 18 V under full channel engagement. True Bypass Architecture, Zero Compromise The Rocket MIDI utilizes a premium-grade, gold-plated, 4PDT mechanical relay switching system rated for 1 million cycles. Each channel’s bypass path is completely isolated — no shared ground planes or shared return traces. Lunastone’s proprietary 'SilentSwitch' algorithm monitors input signal amplitude and only triggers relay actuation when signal level drops below −42 dBFS for ≥12 ms, eliminating audible pop even during high-gain solo passages. Relay timing is factory-calibrated to 8.3 ms activation and 7.1 ms deactivation — faster than industry-standard 12 ms benchmarks set by Boss and Wampler. MIDI Implementation: Beyond Basic Patch Switching MIDI functionality on the Rocket MIDI goes far beyond simple program change reception. It supports full bi-directional communication over both traditional 5-pin DIN and USB-C (Class Compliant MIDI 1.0). The unit ships pre-loaded with 128 user-programmable patches (organized into 8 banks of 16), each storing complete state data: channel selection, gain (0–100%), tone (−12 dB to +12 dB shelving EQ), level (−20 dB to +15 dB), and all active modulation parameters. Patch recall latency is measured at 14.2 ms average — verified using Roland UM-ONE MKII interface and Ablet
